# MEV sandwiching and protection on Solana

# MEV sandwiching and protection on Solana — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for MEV sandwiching and protection on Solana. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Sandwiching is the harmful subset of MEV, not all of it. The Solana docs say much Solana MEV is atomic arbitrage, which corrects price differences across DEXs and is generally beneficial. Marinade draws the same line: beneficial MEV such as arbitrage improves market health, while sandwiching 'is predatory'. (high confidence) — https://solana.com/docs/defi/mev-protection · keywords: MEV sandwiching and protection on Solana · also: https://app.marinade.finance/learn/how-marinade-is-making-sandwiching-validators-pay

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Solana has no public mempool. Transactions are forwarded to upcoming leaders, which limits pre-inclusion visibility but does not remove it. From Jito's launch until March 2024, a Jito relayer held each transaction up to 200 ms so searchers could see it, which acted as a mempool for a subset of transactions. Jito shut that mempool down in March 2024 and named sandwiching as the main reason. (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.28115 · keywords: MEV sandwiching and protection on Solana · also: https://cnitarot.github.io/papers/imc26_solana.pdf, https://helius.dev/blog/solana-mev-report
- [statement] Victims are mostly traders who accept high slippage on thin-liquidity tokens, often through Telegram bots and memecoin apps. Helius says memecoin traders set high slippage to land fast and favour Telegram bots. Marinade says attacks 'primarily target high-slippage trades from Telegram trading bots'. Ghost found that buys of new low-cap tokens are the most likely wide-sandwich targets (low liquidity, high default slippage, speed over price). Bitquery found 96% of detected attacks on Pump.fun's launch curve and PumpSwap. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-12) — https://helius.dev/blog/solana-mev-report · keywords: MEV sandwiching and protection on Solana · also: https://app.marinade.finance/learn/how-marinade-is-making-sandwiching-validators-pay, https://threadreaderapp.com/thread/1978555200802885699, https://cryptoslate.com/solana-sandwich-bots-took-29-7-million-before-costs-bitquery-estimates/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The Helius report lists mitigation designs beyond flags: Jupiter dynamic slippage (Aug 2024), Jito-only MEV Protect modes at slightly higher fees, RFQ swaps (Kamino Swap, JupiterZ) that avoid on-chain slippage but suit illiquid tokens poorly, sandwich-resistant AMMs (Ellipsis Labs Plasma, still crossable at slot boundaries), and Paladin (about 80 validators, about 6% of stake). It warns that validator whitelists risk a semi-permissioned, censored network. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-01-15) — https://helius.dev/blog/solana-mev-report
- [statement] Bundle protection can fail on uncled blocks. When a leader's block is skipped, any party that received it may rebroadcast bundle transactions, which then land through the normal banking stage without bundle atomicity or revert protection. Jito advises pre- and post-account checks, putting the tip instruction in the same transaction as the main logic, and warns that standalone tip transactions raise exposure to 'uncle bandit' cases. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnsend/
- [statement] Bitquery estimated $29.7 million of gross sandwich extraction on Solana between 30 October 2025 and 7 October 2026: 6,850,144 attacks by 2,545 bot wallets against 2,154,994 distinct wallets. The figure is gross. It values SOL at the minute of each attack and does not net out costs. In a separate 63-attack sample, bots kept 68% of gross proceeds and 18 attacks lost money after costs. Pump.fun's launch curve and PumpSwap held 96% of detected attacks. Bitquery says chain records cannot prove a bot saw an order beforehand, and some matching wallets may be fast traders. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-12) — https://cryptoslate.com/solana-sandwich-bots-took-29-7-million-before-costs-bitquery-estimates/
- [statement] Tight slippage is the first-line defense, but not a guarantee. A sandwich can take at most the price move the victim's slippage allows (Chorus One's model), and the Solana docs call tight slippage 'the single most effective defense'. Bitquery's observational data on Jupiter routes through Pump.fun and PumpSwap shows trades allowing 20%-50% slippage were sandwiched 14 times as often as trades under 3%. The rates were not monotonic: trades under 0.5% were hit more often than trades at 1%-3%, and the 50%-and-above band was hit less than the 20%-50% band. A tight limit also makes volatile swaps fail more often. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-12) — https://solana.com/docs/defi/mev-protection · keywords: MEV sandwiching and protection on Solana · also: https://chorus.one/articles/analyzing-mev-instances-on-solana-part-1, https://cryptoslate.com/solana-sandwich-bots-took-29-7-million-before-costs-bitquery-estimates/
- [statement] Ghost's Anti-Sandwich Toolkit is an on-chain guard that reacts when a transaction is routed to a flagged validator. A 192-slot look-ahead window is kept as a 48-bit bitmap, one bit per 4-slot leader chunk. The program can abort with custom error 100 if any targeted slot's leader is flagged, or patch a Jupiter instruction with a fallback slippage and forward it by CPI. The README calls it 'a minimal proof-of-concept' and says it is experimental software that has not been audited. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tryghostxyz/anti-sandwich/main/README.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Solana has no global public mempool: clients forward transactions straight to upcoming leaders, and unprocessed transactions expire after about 150 blocks (~1 minute). The Solana docs say this shrinks the MEV surface compared with public-mempool chains. It does not remove it, because a sandwich only needs someone with early sight of the victim's order (a leader, an RPC or relay, or an app). (high confidence) — https://solana.com/docs/defi/mev-protection · keywords: MEV sandwiching and protection on Solana · also: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.28115, https://cnitarot.github.io/papers/imc26_solana.pdf, https://chorus.one/articles/analyzing-mev-instances-on-solana-part-1

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Slippage tolerance caps what a sandwich can take but does not prevent it. The Solana docs call limiting slippage the single most effective defense. Gerzon et al. cite prior work showing slippage acts as a cap, not a block. Helius and Ghost note that memecoin traders accept high slippage to land fast, which is what attackers exploit. (high confidence) — https://solana.com/docs/defi/mev-protection · keywords: MEV sandwiching and protection on Solana · also: https://cnitarot.github.io/papers/imc26_solana.pdf, https://helius.dev/blog/solana-mev-report, https://threadreaderapp.com/thread/1978555200802885699
